1	name: Docs Preview
2	
3	on:
4	  pull_request:
5	    paths:
6	      - 'packages/**'
7	      - 'composer.json'
8	      - 'composer.lock'
9	      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
10	      - '.github/workflows/docs-preview.yml'
11	    types:
12	      - opened
13	      - synchronize
14	      - reopened
15	      - closed
16	
17	permissions:
18	  contents: read
19	
20	concurrency:
21	  group: package-docs-publish
22	  cancel-in-progress: false
23	
24	env:
25	  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
26	  DOCS_BRANCH: gh-pages
27	
28	jobs:
29	  build:
30	    if: github.event.action != 'closed'
31	    name: Generate documentation for all packages
32	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
33	    timeout-minutes: 15
34	    steps:
35	      - name: Check out the repository
36	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
37	        with:
38	          fetch-depth: 0
39	      - name: Set up PHP
40	        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
41	        with:
42	          php-version: '8.3'
43	          extensions: gd, mbstring, pcntl, mysqli, pdo, pdo_mysql, pdo_pgsql, pdo_sqlite
44	          coverage: none
45	      - name: Install the root project's locked dependencies
46	        run: |
47	          composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
48	          composer install --prefer-dist --no-progress
49	          composer check-platform-reqs
50	      - name: Generate documentation
51	        env:
52	          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
53	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
54	        run: |
55	          repository="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}"
56	          # The generated statement models of the sql-semantics database packages are documented on the published site but left out of the comparison: diffing them class by class exceeds the memory limit and says nothing a reviewer needs.
57	          composer docgen -- --diff="$BASE_SHA" --exclude='packages/sql-semantics-*/resources/*' --base-url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
58	      - name: Upload the documentation site
59	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
60	        with:
61	          name: package-docs
62	          path: build/docs/
63	          include-hidden-files: true
64	          if-no-files-found: error
65	
66	  preview:
67	    needs: build
68	    name: Generate and publish the pull request preview
69	    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
70	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
71	    timeout-minutes: 30
72	    permissions:
73	      contents: write
74	      pages: write
75	      pull-requests: write
76	    steps:
77	      - name: Download the complete documentation site
78	        uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0
79	        with:
80	          name: package-docs
81	          path: build/docs
82	
83	      - name: Check out the documentation branch
84	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
85	        with:
86	          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
87	          path: .docs-branch
88	
89	      - name: Publish the preview
90	        working-directory: .docs-branch
91	        env:
92	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
93	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
94	        run: |
95	          set -euo pipefail
96	
97	          mkdir -p "pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
98	          rsync -a --checksum --delete ../build/docs/ "pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"
99	          touch .nojekyll
100	
101	          git add --all
102	          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
103	            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch already serves this preview."
104	            exit 0
105	          fi
106	
107	          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
108	            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
109	            commit --message "docs: preview pull request #${PR_NUMBER} at ${HEAD_SHA}"
110	          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"
111	
112	      - name: Build GitHub Pages and wait for publication
113	        env:
114	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
115	        run: |
116	          set -euo pipefail
117	
118	          expected_sha="$(git -C .docs-branch rev-parse HEAD)"
119	          gh api --method POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds" > /dev/null
120	          for attempt in {1..60}; do
121	            build="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds/latest")"
122	            if [ "$(jq -r .commit <<< "$build")" = "$expected_sha" ]; then
123	              case "$(jq -r .status <<< "$build")" in
124	                built) exit 0 ;;

name: Docs Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'packages/**'
      - 'composer.json'
      - 'composer.lock'
      - '.github/workflows/docs.yml'
      - '.github/workflows/docs-preview.yml'
    types:
      - opened
      - synchronize
      - reopened
      - closed

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: package-docs-publish
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
  DOCS_BRANCH: gh-pages

jobs:
  build:
    if: github.event.action != 'closed'
    name: Generate documentation for all packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: '8.3'
          extensions: gd, mbstring, pcntl, mysqli, pdo, pdo_mysql, pdo_pgsql, pdo_sqlite
          coverage: none
      - name: Install the root project's locked dependencies
        run: |
          composer validate --strict --no-check-publish
          composer install --prefer-dist --no-progress
          composer check-platform-reqs
      - name: Generate documentation
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          repository="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY,,}"
          # The generated statement models of the sql-semantics database packages are documented on the published site but left out of the comparison: diffing them class by class exceeds the memory limit and says nothing a reviewer needs.
          composer docgen -- --diff="$BASE_SHA" --exclude='packages/sql-semantics-*/resources/*' --base-url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
      - name: Upload the documentation site
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        with:
          name: package-docs
          path: build/docs/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error

  preview:
    needs: build
    name: Generate and publish the pull request preview
    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pages: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Download the complete documentation site
        uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0
        with:
          name: package-docs
          path: build/docs

      - name: Check out the documentation branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
          path: .docs-branch

      - name: Publish the preview
        working-directory: .docs-branch
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          mkdir -p "pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
          rsync -a --checksum --delete ../build/docs/ "pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"
          touch .nojekyll

          git add --all
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch already serves this preview."
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message "docs: preview pull request #${PR_NUMBER} at ${HEAD_SHA}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

      - name: Build GitHub Pages and wait for publication
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          expected_sha="$(git -C .docs-branch rev-parse HEAD)"
          gh api --method POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds" > /dev/null
          for attempt in {1..60}; do
            build="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds/latest")"
            if [ "$(jq -r .commit <<< "$build")" = "$expected_sha" ]; then
              case "$(jq -r .status <<< "$build")" in
                built) exit 0 ;;
                # Pages can replace a cancelled build for this same commit.
                errored) jq .error <<< "$build" >&2 ;;
              esac
            fi
            sleep 10
          done
          echo 'Timed out waiting for GitHub Pages publication.' >&2
          exit 1

      - name: Comment the preview link on the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          repository="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
          preview_url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"

          comment_file="$(mktemp)"
          cat > "$comment_file" <<EOF
          <!-- package-docgen-preview -->
          **Documentation preview:** [All packages](${preview_url})

          Generated in diff mode against ${BASE_REF}. Use **Off**, **Diff**, or
          **Changes** at the top of the page to select the documentation view.

          Updated for ${HEAD_SHA}. The preview is removed when this pull request is closed.
          EOF
          comment_id="$(gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments" \
            --jq '.[] | select(.user.login == "github-actions[bot]" and (.body | startswith("<!-- package-docgen-preview -->"))) | .id' | tail -n 1)"
          if [ -n "$comment_id" ]; then
            gh api --method PATCH "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${comment_id}" -F "body=@${comment_file}"
          else
            gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --body-file "$comment_file"
          fi

  cleanup:
    name: Remove the pull request preview
    if: github.event.action == 'closed' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pages: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out the documentation branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}

      - name: Remove the preview
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          rm -rf "pr/${PR_NUMBER}"

          git add --all
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch carries no preview of this pull request."
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message "docs: remove the preview of pull request #${PR_NUMBER}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

      - name: Build GitHub Pages and wait for publication
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          expected_sha="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
          gh api --method POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds" > /dev/null
          for attempt in {1..60}; do
            build="$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/pages/builds/latest")"
            if [ "$(jq -r .commit <<< "$build")" = "$expected_sha" ]; then
              case "$(jq -r .status <<< "$build")" in
                built) exit 0 ;;
                # Pages can replace a cancelled build for this same commit.
                errored) jq .error <<< "$build" >&2 ;;
              esac
            fi
            sleep 10
          done
          echo 'Timed out waiting for GitHub Pages publication.' >&2
          exit 1

      - name: Note the removal on the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          comment_id="$(gh api --paginate "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR_NUMBER}/comments" \
            --jq '.[] | select(.user.login == "github-actions[bot]" and (.body | startswith("<!-- package-docgen-preview -->"))) | .id' | tail -n 1)"
          if [ -n "$comment_id" ]; then
            comment_file="$(mktemp)"
            cat > "$comment_file" <<'EOF'
          <!-- package-docgen-preview -->
          The documentation preview of this pull request has been removed.
          EOF
            gh api --method PATCH "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${comment_id}" -F "body=@${comment_file}"
          fi

name: Docs

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - REPLACE_WITH_DEFAULT_BRANCH
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
  DOCS_BRANCH: REPLACE_WITH_DOCS_BRANCH

jobs:
  publish:
    name: Generate and publish the documentation site
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out the repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: 'REPLACE_WITH_DOCGEN_JOB_PHP'
          extensions: REPLACE_WITH_REQUIRED_EXTENSIONS
          coverage: pcov

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: REPLACE_WITH_DEPENDENCY_MODE
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: REPLACE_WITH_LOCK_REQUIREMENT

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Restore the DocGen cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: build/docgen-cache
          key: docgen-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('REPLACE_WITH_SELECTED_LOCK_FILE') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            docgen-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('REPLACE_WITH_SELECTED_LOCK_FILE') }}-
            docgen-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Generate the coverage report the site reads
        run: vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-xml build/coverage-xml

      - name: Generate the documentation
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          repository="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
          vendor/bin/docgen --coverage=build/coverage-xml \
            --base-url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}"

      - name: Check out the documentation branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
          path: .docs-branch

      - name: Publish the site
        working-directory: .docs-branch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          rsync -a --checksum --delete --exclude '/.git/' --exclude '/pr/' --exclude '/CNAME' ../build/docs/ ./

          git add --all
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch already serves this documentation."
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message "docs: generate from ${GITHUB_SHA}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-readme
3	description: >-
4	  Set up a minimal README.md for a PHP project: badges, a one-paragraph
5	  overview, Requirements, Getting Started, and License. Use when asked to
6	  create, trim, or restructure README.md, add badges for CI workflows, a docs
7	  site, PHP versions, license, Packagist, or DeepWiki, or link the repository's
8	  DeepWiki page.
9	---
10	
11	# Setup README
12	
13	This skill writes the product README the way php-ai-toolkit projects keep it:
14	the least a reader needs to decide whether to install the package and to run it
15	once. Everything else lives in `docs/` or the generated documentation site.
16	
17	Use this skill only when the user explicitly asks to create or change
18	`README.md`. Applying the toolkit, adding a workflow, or publishing
19	documentation is not permission to rewrite the product README; the other setup
20	skills say the same. If `README.md` already exists, treat it as product-owned:
21	keep the facts and prose in it, add or change only what the request names, and
22	ask before removing a section the user did not mention.
23	
24	## Discover Project Facts
25	
26	Read these before writing:
27	
28	- `composer.json`: `name`, `description`, `require.php`, the `require` entries
29	  a user must provide themselves (extensions, external tools, framework peers),
30	  `license`, `homepage`, and `support.docs`.
31	- `LICENSE`: the license named by the badge and the closing section.
32	- `.github/workflows/*.yml`: every workflow that runs on the default branch is
33	  a status badge candidate.
34	- The docs workflow, the `gh-pages` branch, or `support.docs`: whether a
35	  documentation site is published and at which address.
36	- Packagist: whether `composer require` works without a `repositories` entry.
37	  Check `https://packagist.org/packages/<vendor>/<package>` rather than
38	  assuming; a package that is not there needs the VCS repository entry in
39	  Getting Started.
40	- The default branch name, for `?branch=` on workflow badges.
41	- In a monorepo, the package directory: badges link to the repository's
42	  workflows and to the package's own documentation path.
43	
44	## Template
45	
46	Read the template from
47	`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-readme/README.md` and
48	replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` from project evidence. Do not copy this
49	repository's badges, versions, or wording.
50	
51	| Placeholder | Value |
52	|-------------|-------|
53	| `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` | The package or repository name. |
54	| `{{BADGES}}` | The badge block from the Badges section, one badge per line. |
55	| `{{OVERVIEW}}` | One paragraph: what the package is, who it is for, and the one thing that distinguishes it. |
56	| `{{PHP_CONSTRAINT}}` | `require.php` written for people, such as `8.1 or higher`. |
57	| `{{ADDITIONAL_REQUIREMENTS}}` | One bullet per extension, external tool, or peer the package cannot install itself; remove the line when there are none. |
58	| `{{INSTALL_COMMAND}}` | The `composer require` line, with `--dev` for development tools and the `repositories` entry first when the package is not on Packagist. |
59	| `{{GETTING_STARTED_EXAMPLE}}` | The shortest complete example that does something useful: a code block for a library, the command and its output for a CLI. |
60	| `{{LICENSE_NAME}}` | The license name, such as `MIT License`. |
61	
62	## Structure
63	
64	The README has a title, a badge block, one paragraph, and three sections:
65	Requirements, Getting Started, and License. The overview is prose, not a
66	feature list.

---
name: setup-toolkit-readme
description: >-
  Set up a minimal README.md for a PHP project: badges, a one-paragraph
  overview, Requirements, Getting Started, and License. Use when asked to
  create, trim, or restructure README.md, add badges for CI workflows, a docs
  site, PHP versions, license, Packagist, or DeepWiki, or link the repository's
  DeepWiki page.
---

# Setup README

This skill writes the product README the way php-ai-toolkit projects keep it:
the least a reader needs to decide whether to install the package and to run it
once. Everything else lives in `docs/` or the generated documentation site.

Use this skill only when the user explicitly asks to create or change
`README.md`. Applying the toolkit, adding a workflow, or publishing
documentation is not permission to rewrite the product README; the other setup
skills say the same. If `README.md` already exists, treat it as product-owned:
keep the facts and prose in it, add or change only what the request names, and
ask before removing a section the user did not mention.

## Discover Project Facts

Read these before writing:

- `composer.json`: `name`, `description`, `require.php`, the `require` entries
  a user must provide themselves (extensions, external tools, framework peers),
  `license`, `homepage`, and `support.docs`.
- `LICENSE`: the license named by the badge and the closing section.
- `.github/workflows/*.yml`: every workflow that runs on the default branch is
  a status badge candidate.
- The docs workflow, the `gh-pages` branch, or `support.docs`: whether a
  documentation site is published and at which address.
- Packagist: whether `composer require` works without a `repositories` entry.
  Check `https://packagist.org/packages/<vendor>/<package>` rather than
  assuming; a package that is not there needs the VCS repository entry in
  Getting Started.
- The default branch name, for `?branch=` on workflow badges.
- In a monorepo, the package directory: badges link to the repository's
  workflows and to the package's own documentation path.

## Template

Read the template from
`vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-readme/README.md` and
replace every `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` from project evidence. Do not copy this
repository's badges, versions, or wording.

| Placeholder | Value |
|-------------|-------|
| `{{PROJECT_NAME}}` | The package or repository name. |
| `{{BADGES}}` | The badge block from the Badges section, one badge per line. |
| `{{OVERVIEW}}` | One paragraph: what the package is, who it is for, and the one thing that distinguishes it. |
| `{{PHP_CONSTRAINT}}` | `require.php` written for people, such as `8.1 or higher`. |
| `{{ADDITIONAL_REQUIREMENTS}}` | One bullet per extension, external tool, or peer the package cannot install itself; remove the line when there are none. |
| `{{INSTALL_COMMAND}}` | The `composer require` line, with `--dev` for development tools and the `repositories` entry first when the package is not on Packagist. |
| `{{GETTING_STARTED_EXAMPLE}}` | The shortest complete example that does something useful: a code block for a library, the command and its output for a CLI. |
| `{{LICENSE_NAME}}` | The license name, such as `MIT License`. |

## Structure

The README has a title, a badge block, one paragraph, and three sections:
Requirements, Getting Started, and License. The overview is prose, not a
feature list.

Add a further section only when the reader cannot use the package without it:
a table of supported syntaxes or drivers, a CLI's `--help` output, or the shape
of a configuration file. Name that section for its content and keep it between
Getting Started and License. Do not add Features, Architecture, Contributing,
Changelog, Roadmap, or Acknowledgements sections; architecture and tooling
belong to `docs/` and the generated site, and the docs badge is the link to
them.

Prefer leaving information out over compressing it. A reader who needs more
follows the docs badge.

## Badges

Add every badge the project can back with a real target, in this order:

1. The documentation site, when DocGen or another generator publishes one:
   ```markdown
   [![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-<package>-0969da?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/)
   ```
2. One status badge per workflow that runs on the default branch (CI, docs,
   Context7, and so on), pinned to that branch:
   ```markdown
   [![CI](https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=<default-branch>)](https://github.com/<owner>/<repository>/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
   ```
3. The Packagist version, only when the package is published there:
   ```markdown
   [![Packagist](https://img.shields.io/packagist/v/<vendor>/<package>)](https://packagist.org/packages/<vendor>/<package>)
   ```
4. The supported PHP versions, derived from `require.php` and the CI matrix:
   ```markdown
   [![PHP](https://img.shields.io/badge/php-8.1%20%7C%208.2%20%7C%208.3-777bb4?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://www.php.net/)
   ```
5. The license, from `composer.json` and `LICENSE`:
   ```markdown
   [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)](LICENSE)
   ```
6. DeepWiki, for every public repository, as described below.

A badge must point at something that exists: no workflow badge for a workflow
the project does not have, no Packagist badge for a VCS-only package, no
coverage badge without a coverage service. Add a badge in the same change that
adds its target, never ahead of it.

## DeepWiki

DeepWiki (https://deepwiki.com) generates a browsable wiki and a question
interface for a public GitHub repository. Add its badge to every public
repository:

```markdown
[![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/<owner>/<repository>)
```

The link is the repository, not a package path: DeepWiki indexes repositories,
so a package inside a monorepo links to the monorepo's page.

Indexing is free for public repositories but does not happen by itself. Open
`https://deepwiki.com/<owner>/<repository>`; if the page offers to index the
repository instead of showing a wiki, ask the user to submit it there. The badge
renders before indexing finishes, but the link shows nothing useful until then,
so say so in the delivery. DeepWiki for private repositories is a paid Devin
feature; report that instead of adding a badge that leads to a sign-in page.

## Verification

After editing:

```bash
git diff --check
```

Then check that every absolute link and badge in the README resolves:

```bash
grep -o 'https://[^)"]*' README.md | sort -u | while read -r url; do
  if curl --silent --fail --head --location --output /dev/null "$url"; then
    echo "ok   $url"
  else
    echo "FAIL $url"
  fi
done
```

Confirm the install command works as written from an empty directory when the
package is public, and that the Getting Started example runs against the
installed package. Report anything that could not be executed locally.

1	---
2	name: setup-toolkit-docgen
3	description: >-
4	  Set up DocGen static documentation generation for a PHP project. Use when
5	  asked to configure docgen, its command line options, API documentation
6	  generation, a docs.rs-style documentation site, GitHub Pages hosting,
7	  multi-package or monorepo documentation, documenting vendor packages,
8	  architecture layer visualization from deptrac, per-method test coverage
9	  references in documentation, executable doctest examples in docs,
10	  documentation that compares two git revisions, incremental documentation
11	  builds with a parse and page cache, per-pull-request documentation previews,
12	  or Composer scripts and CI jobs that publish generated PHP documentation.
13	---
14	
15	# Setup DocGen (Static Documentation Site)
16	
17	This skill configures `docgen`, the php-ai-toolkit CLI that generates a dense, fully cross-linked static HTML
18	documentation site — complete types, interface implementations, call sites, architecture layers, coverage-backed
19	test references, runnable doctest examples, and an optional comparison of two git revisions — for the composer
20	packages of a project.
21	
22	## Prerequisites
23	
24	Inspect `composer.json` before configuring:
25	
26	- Confirm the target project requires `k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit`.
27	- Read the Composer PSR-4 autoload maps; they define exactly what gets documented.
28	- Check whether the repository is a monorepo (`packages/*/composer.json`) or a single package.
29	- Check for an existing documentation step, such as a `docgen` Composer script or a docs workflow.
30	
31	Install the toolkit if missing:
32	
33	```bash
34	composer require --dev k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit
35	```
36	
37	The unversioned requirement is intentional for a new install: Composer should
38	select the newest stable toolkit release compatible with the target project. Check
39	current package metadata and the target's PHP/dependency graph first. If the toolkit
40	is already constrained, update its lock to the newest admitted release and preserve
41	an intentional pin unless changing that policy is in scope. Never copy this
42	repository's root constraint or lock resolution.
43	
44	The target repository's `docs/` and README are product surfaces. DocGen consumes
45	their existing product documentation; setup does not add developer-tooling pages
46	there. Apart from an explicitly approved public docs badge, configure the generator
47	through Composer and workflows only.
48	
49	## Configuration
50	
51	**DocGen has no configuration file.** A run is configured by its options alone, so the command that generated a site
52	is the whole description of that site — which is what lets a CI job pass the values only it knows, such as the
53	address the site is published at. Write the project's own settings into a Composer script, and leave the rest to the
54	job that calls it.
55	
56	| Option | Default | Meaning |
57	|--------|---------|---------|
58	| `--packages=GLOBS` | `.` and `packages/*` | Directory globs probed for a `composer.json`; each hit becomes a documented package. |
59	| `--vendor[=GLOBS]` | none | Composer package-name globs (`acme/*`, not directory names) of installed **runtime** dependencies to document alongside the project; bare `--vendor` means all of them. |
60	| `--vendor-dev[=GLOBS]` | none | The same for installed **dev** dependencies; leave it off unless the test tooling itself needs documenting. |
61	| `--exclude=GLOBS` | none | Path globs, relative to the project root, pruned from source scanning. |
62	| `--output=DIR` | `build/docs` | Site output directory. |
63	| `--title=TEXT` | the root package name | Site title. |
64	| `--deptrac=FILE` | `deptrac.yaml` when present | Deptrac configuration the architecture graph and the layer badges are read from. |
65	| `--coverage=DIR` | none | PHPUnit `--coverage-xml` report directory; links every method to the test cases covering it. |
66	| `--base-url=URL` | none | Absolute address the site is published at, without a trailing slash. Pass it where the site is published from; it is what the canonical links and the social preview are written from. |
67	| `--repository=URL` | what the root `composer.json` declares | Absolute address of the repository the project lives in, which every page links back to. Pass it only to override `support.source` or `homepage`. |
68	| `--cache-dir=DIR` | `build/docgen-cache` | Directory the parsed sources and written pages are remembered in; `--no-cache` turns caching off for one run. Keep it outside the output directory. |
69	
70	Every option that takes `GLOBS` reads a comma-separated list and may be repeated, which adds to what the earlier
71	occurrences named. `docgen --help` lists these together with the run options (`--jobs`, `--memory-limit`,
72	`--serve`, `--diff`, `--clear-cache`).
73	
74	## Scope Semantics
75	
76	The documented unit is the composer package: production autoload sources become API pages while `autoload-dev`
77	sources become linkable source pages only, so test references stay navigable without widening the API surface.
78	Page content and design are fixed by the generator on purpose — only the scope is configurable.
79	
80	## Adapting to the Project
81	
82	- Single-package repositories need no `--packages`; the default `packages/*` glob simply matches nothing.
83	- For one package in a monorepo, set `--packages` explicitly to that package.
84	  Use one working directory for normal and diff runs, deriving the executable,
85	  Deptrac, coverage, output, and cache paths from it. Confirm neither run discovers
86	  sibling packages merely because it starts at the repository root.
87	- Add `--exclude` globs for fixture directories that contain intentionally invalid PHP (for example
88	  `--exclude=tests/Fixture/*`).
89	- Leave `--vendor` and `--vendor-dev` off for a product-only site, even when
90	  dependency types occur in public signatures. When dependency documentation is
91	  requested, select specific package-name globs such as `--vendor=acme/*`; bare
92	  `--vendor` adds every runtime dependency. Unmatched globs and packages shipping
93	  only a PHAR produce warnings.
94	- Documenting many vendor packages needs memory: the run raises a limit below 512M automatically, and
95	  `--memory-limit=1G` handles very large dependency trees.
96	- When the project runs deptrac, keep `deptrac.yaml` at the root so the architecture graph appears automatically.
97	- Generate coverage with `--coverage-xml build/coverage-xml` and pass `--coverage=build/coverage-xml` so every method
98	  links the test cases that cover it.
99	- Runs are incremental by default: the next run parses only the sources that changed and rewrites only the pages
100	  that changed, and reports what it reused (`Cache: 861 of 862 sources and 1365 of 1411 pages reused`). The site is
101	  the same site a full run writes, byte for byte. Use `--no-cache` to prove that on demand, `--clear-cache` to start
102	  over, and `--cache-dir=DIR` to keep the cache elsewhere. Add the cache directory to `.gitignore`.
103	- In CI, restore the cache directory between runs (for example with `actions/cache` keyed on `composer.lock` and the
104	  toolkit version) so a documentation job costs the size of the change rather than the size of the project.
105	- To review what a branch changed, generate the site in diff mode: `--diff=<default-branch>` compares the working tree against
106	  the target's default branch, and `--diff=v1.0.0..HEAD` compares two revisions. The site then marks additions and removals down to the single
107	  argument of a declaration and offers three display modes — the plain documentation, the marked documentation, and
108	  the changes alone. Diff mode needs a git working tree and analyzes both revisions, so it takes about twice as long.
109	
110	## Recommended Composer Scripts
111	
112	The scripts are where the project's own settings live, because there is no configuration file to keep them in.
113	Write the settings once in `docgen`, and let the other scripts add to it:
114	
115	```json
116	{
117	    "scripts": {
118	        "docgen": "docgen --exclude='tests/Fixture/*' --coverage=build/coverage-xml",
119	        "docgen:serve": "@docgen --serve",
120	        "docgen:diff": "@docgen --diff=REPLACE_WITH_DEFAULT_BRANCH --serve",
121	        "docgen:fresh": "@docgen --no-cache"
122	    }
123	}
124	```
125	
126	Quote a glob that a shell would otherwise expand, as `'tests/Fixture/*'` above. A caller adds to the script's
127	options with `composer docgen -- --base-url=https://example.github.io/project`, which is how a CI job passes what
128	only it knows.
129	
130	Do not add `docgen` to `lint`; it is a generator, not a check.
131	
132	## GitHub Pages Publishing
133	
134	The site is fully static and already contains `.nojekyll`, so publishing it means committing the output directory
135	to a branch that GitHub Pages serves. This skill ships two workflow templates for that, and **which of them to
136	install is the user's decision — ask before writing any workflow file**:
137	
138	| Answer | What to install |
139	|--------|-----------------|
140	| No CI publishing | Nothing; `docgen` stays a local command. |
141	| Publish the default branch | `docs.yml` only. |
142	| Publish and preview pull requests | `docs.yml` and `docs-preview.yml`. |
143	
144	Never install `docs-preview.yml` without `docs.yml`: the preview workflow writes only below `pr/<number>/` and
145	expects the site workflow to own the root of the branch.
146	
147	Read the templates from `vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-docgen/docs.yml` and
148	`docs-preview.yml` and apply them as `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `.github/workflows/docs-preview.yml`.
149	
150	Both contain `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinels for project-derived PHP, extensions, lock
151	policy, and branch values. Replace every sentinel before installing either
152	workflow; do not substitute values from this repository merely to make the YAML
153	complete.
154	
155	- `docs.yml` runs on pushes to the default branch: it generates the site and syncs it to the root of the `gh-pages`
156	  branch, keeping `pr/` and `CNAME`.
157	- `docs-preview.yml` runs on pull requests: it generates the site in diff mode against the base commit, publishes it
158	  to `pr/<number>/`, comments the link on the pull request, and removes that directory when the pull request closes.
159	  Pull requests from forks are skipped, because their token cannot write to the branch.
160	
161	Adapt both to the project before applying:
162	
163	- Use the highest PHP version in the project's support matrix unless DocGen cannot
164	  run there, and add the lock-file step the project's CI uses. For versioned locks,
165	  select `composer.lock.php-<chosen-minor>`; for a normal lock, add no copy step.
166	  Require the selected lock file to exist and run `composer check-platform-reqs`
167	  after installation.
168	- Derive extensions from Composer platform requirements plus the workflow itself:
169	  coverage needs pcov or Xdebug, social images need GD with FreeType, and a
170	  parallel coverage script needs pcntl. Do not copy the template list blindly.
171	- Match the generation command to the project: the Composer script, or `vendor/bin/docgen` with the project's own
172	  options spelled out.
173	- Match the `on.push.branches` entry to the default branch, and `DOCS_BRANCH` to the branch Pages serves.
174	- Keep the action pins as full commit SHAs, the per-job `contents: write`
175	  permission, and `pull_request` (never `pull_request_target`) as the preview trigger.
176	
177	The default-branch and pull-request workflows must generate the same product site.
178	Use the same project Composer coverage and DocGen scripts in both, adding only the
179	event-derived base URL and `--diff` value for a preview. Omitting coverage, packages,
180	exclusions, architecture input, or other content from previews is a separate human
181	speed-versus-parity decision; do not infer it from the template or a slow first run.
182	Job timeouts, memory, and cache retention are operational values to measure, not
183	quality policy.
184	
185	Pass `--base-url` with the published address at the same time, because that is what makes a shared link render as a
186	card: every page then carries its canonical link, its own description, and the Open Graph tags, and the run draws
187	`assets/og-image.png` from the site title and the project description (needs `ext-gd`; without it the pages simply
188	carry no image). Both workflow templates derive that address from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, so a fork or a rename needs
189	no edit. If the user explicitly approves changing the product README, add a docs
190	badge that links to the site, the way docs.rs does:
191	
192	```markdown
193	[![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-<package>-0969da?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/)
194	```
195	
196	Close the loop the other way too: the site links back to the repository from every page, reading the address from
197	`support.source` (then `homepage`) in the package's `composer.json`. Add those entries where the project declares
198	neither — `support.docs` and `homepage` can point at the published site — and pass `--repository` only to override
199	what the manifests declare.
200	
201	Tell the user about the one-time repository setup the workflows do not do:
202	
203	```bash
204	git switch --orphan gh-pages
205	git commit --allow-empty -m 'docs: create the documentation branch'
206	git push -u origin gh-pages
207	git switch <default-branch>
208	```
209	
210	Then set Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source to "Deploy from a branch", branch `gh-pages`, folder
211	`/ (root)`. The site is served at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/`, and previews at
212	`https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/pr/<number>/`.
213	
214	## Verification
215	
216	After applying:
217	
218	```bash
219	composer docgen
220	```
221	
222	Exit codes:
223	
224	- `0`: documentation generated
225	- `2`: configuration or runtime error
226	
227	Then preview locally with `vendor/bin/docgen --serve` and spot-check the index page, one class page, and search.
228	
229	Check the generated package list and source links in normal and diff output. After
230	narrowing scope, regenerate with the existing cache and verify removed package
231	pages disappear; publishing must delete stale output too while preserving the
232	preview directories owned by the other workflow.
233	
234	When a workflow was installed, check it too, and say plainly that the publishing itself is only observable after the
235	workflow runs on the default branch:
236	
237	```bash
238	go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@latest .github/workflows/docs.yml
239	```
240	
241	## References
242	
243	- [DocGen](vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/docs/docgen.md) — CLI behavior, scope semantics, caching, analysis, and output.

is already constrained, update its lock to the newest admitted release and preserve
an intentional pin unless changing that policy is in scope. Never copy this
repository's root constraint or lock resolution.

The target repository's `docs/` and README are product surfaces. DocGen consumes
their existing product documentation; setup does not add developer-tooling pages
there. Apart from an explicitly approved public docs badge, configure the generator
through Composer and workflows only.

## Configuration

**DocGen has no configuration file.** A run is configured by its options alone, so the command that generated a site
is the whole description of that site — which is what lets a CI job pass the values only it knows, such as the
address the site is published at. Write the project's own settings into a Composer script, and leave the rest to the
job that calls it.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `--packages=GLOBS` | `.` and `packages/*` | Directory globs probed for a `composer.json`; each hit becomes a documented package. |
| `--vendor[=GLOBS]` | none | Composer package-name globs (`acme/*`, not directory names) of installed **runtime** dependencies to document alongside the project; bare `--vendor` means all of them. |
| `--vendor-dev[=GLOBS]` | none | The same for installed **dev** dependencies; leave it off unless the test tooling itself needs documenting. |
| `--exclude=GLOBS` | none | Path globs, relative to the project root, pruned from source scanning. |
| `--output=DIR` | `build/docs` | Site output directory. |
| `--title=TEXT` | the root package name | Site title. |
| `--deptrac=FILE` | `deptrac.yaml` when present | Deptrac configuration the architecture graph and the layer badges are read from. |
| `--coverage=DIR` | none | PHPUnit `--coverage-xml` report directory; links every method to the test cases covering it. |
| `--base-url=URL` | none | Absolute address the site is published at, without a trailing slash. Pass it where the site is published from; it is what the canonical links and the social preview are written from. |
| `--repository=URL` | what the root `composer.json` declares | Absolute address of the repository the project lives in, which every page links back to. Pass it only to override `support.source` or `homepage`. |
| `--cache-dir=DIR` | `build/docgen-cache` | Directory the parsed sources and written pages are remembered in; `--no-cache` turns caching off for one run. Keep it outside the output directory. |

Every option that takes `GLOBS` reads a comma-separated list and may be repeated, which adds to what the earlier
occurrences named. `docgen --help` lists these together with the run options (`--jobs`, `--memory-limit`,
`--serve`, `--diff`, `--clear-cache`).

## Scope Semantics

The documented unit is the composer package: production autoload sources become API pages while `autoload-dev`
sources become linkable source pages only, so test references stay navigable without widening the API surface.
Page content and design are fixed by the generator on purpose — only the scope is configurable.

## Adapting to the Project

- Single-package repositories need no `--packages`; the default `packages/*` glob simply matches nothing.
- For one package in a monorepo, set `--packages` explicitly to that package.
  Use one working directory for normal and diff runs, deriving the executable,
  Deptrac, coverage, output, and cache paths from it. Confirm neither run discovers
  sibling packages merely because it starts at the repository root.
- Add `--exclude` globs for fixture directories that contain intentionally invalid PHP (for example
  `--exclude=tests/Fixture/*`).
- Leave `--vendor` and `--vendor-dev` off for a product-only site, even when
  dependency types occur in public signatures. When dependency documentation is
  requested, select specific package-name globs such as `--vendor=acme/*`; bare
  `--vendor` adds every runtime dependency. Unmatched globs and packages shipping
  only a PHAR produce warnings.
- Documenting many vendor packages needs memory: the run raises a limit below 512M automatically, and
  `--memory-limit=1G` handles very large dependency trees.
- When the project runs deptrac, keep `deptrac.yaml` at the root so the architecture graph appears automatically.
- Generate coverage with `--coverage-xml build/coverage-xml` and pass `--coverage=build/coverage-xml` so every method
  links the test cases that cover it.
- Runs are incremental by default: the next run parses only the sources that changed and rewrites only the pages
  that changed, and reports what it reused (`Cache: 861 of 862 sources and 1365 of 1411 pages reused`). The site is
  the same site a full run writes, byte for byte. Use `--no-cache` to prove that on demand, `--clear-cache` to start
  over, and `--cache-dir=DIR` to keep the cache elsewhere. Add the cache directory to `.gitignore`.
- In CI, restore the cache directory between runs (for example with `actions/cache` keyed on `composer.lock` and the
  toolkit version) so a documentation job costs the size of the change rather than the size of the project.
- To review what a branch changed, generate the site in diff mode: `--diff=<default-branch>` compares the working tree against
  the target's default branch, and `--diff=v1.0.0..HEAD` compares two revisions. The site then marks additions and removals down to the single
  argument of a declaration and offers three display modes — the plain documentation, the marked documentation, and
  the changes alone. Diff mode needs a git working tree and analyzes both revisions, so it takes about twice as long.

## Recommended Composer Scripts

The scripts are where the project's own settings live, because there is no configuration file to keep them in.
Write the settings once in `docgen`, and let the other scripts add to it:

```json
{
    "scripts": {
        "docgen": "docgen --exclude='tests/Fixture/*' --coverage=build/coverage-xml",
        "docgen:serve": "@docgen --serve",
        "docgen:diff": "@docgen --diff=REPLACE_WITH_DEFAULT_BRANCH --serve",
        "docgen:fresh": "@docgen --no-cache"
    }
}
```

Quote a glob that a shell would otherwise expand, as `'tests/Fixture/*'` above. A caller adds to the script's
options with `composer docgen -- --base-url=https://example.github.io/project`, which is how a CI job passes what
only it knows.

Do not add `docgen` to `lint`; it is a generator, not a check.

## GitHub Pages Publishing

The site is fully static and already contains `.nojekyll`, so publishing it means committing the output directory
to a branch that GitHub Pages serves. This skill ships two workflow templates for that, and **which of them to
install is the user's decision — ask before writing any workflow file**:

| Answer | What to install |
|--------|-----------------|
| No CI publishing | Nothing; `docgen` stays a local command. |
| Publish the default branch | `docs.yml` only. |
| Publish and preview pull requests | `docs.yml` and `docs-preview.yml`. |

Never install `docs-preview.yml` without `docs.yml`: the preview workflow writes only below `pr/<number>/` and
expects the site workflow to own the root of the branch.

Read the templates from `vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/skills/setup-toolkit-docgen/docs.yml` and
`docs-preview.yml` and apply them as `.github/workflows/docs.yml` and `.github/workflows/docs-preview.yml`.

Both contain `REPLACE_WITH_*` sentinels for project-derived PHP, extensions, lock
policy, and branch values. Replace every sentinel before installing either
workflow; do not substitute values from this repository merely to make the YAML
complete.

- `docs.yml` runs on pushes to the default branch: it generates the site and syncs it to the root of the `gh-pages`
  branch, keeping `pr/` and `CNAME`.
- `docs-preview.yml` runs on pull requests: it generates the site in diff mode against the base commit, publishes it
  to `pr/<number>/`, comments the link on the pull request, and removes that directory when the pull request closes.
  Pull requests from forks are skipped, because their token cannot write to the branch.

Adapt both to the project before applying:

- Use the highest PHP version in the project's support matrix unless DocGen cannot
  run there, and add the lock-file step the project's CI uses. For versioned locks,
  select `composer.lock.php-<chosen-minor>`; for a normal lock, add no copy step.
  Require the selected lock file to exist and run `composer check-platform-reqs`
  after installation.
- Derive extensions from Composer platform requirements plus the workflow itself:
  coverage needs pcov or Xdebug, social images need GD with FreeType, and a
  parallel coverage script needs pcntl. Do not copy the template list blindly.
- Match the generation command to the project: the Composer script, or `vendor/bin/docgen` with the project's own
  options spelled out.
- Match the `on.push.branches` entry to the default branch, and `DOCS_BRANCH` to the branch Pages serves.
- Keep the action pins as full commit SHAs, the per-job `contents: write`
  permission, and `pull_request` (never `pull_request_target`) as the preview trigger.

The default-branch and pull-request workflows must generate the same product site.
Use the same project Composer coverage and DocGen scripts in both, adding only the
event-derived base URL and `--diff` value for a preview. Omitting coverage, packages,
exclusions, architecture input, or other content from previews is a separate human
speed-versus-parity decision; do not infer it from the template or a slow first run.
Job timeouts, memory, and cache retention are operational values to measure, not
quality policy.

Pass `--base-url` with the published address at the same time, because that is what makes a shared link render as a
card: every page then carries its canonical link, its own description, and the Open Graph tags, and the run draws
`assets/og-image.png` from the site title and the project description (needs `ext-gd`; without it the pages simply
carry no image). Both workflow templates derive that address from `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, so a fork or a rename needs
no edit. If the user explicitly approves changing the product README, add a docs
badge that links to the site, the way docs.rs does:

```markdown
[![docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-<package>-0969da?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/)
```

Close the loop the other way too: the site links back to the repository from every page, reading the address from
`support.source` (then `homepage`) in the package's `composer.json`. Add those entries where the project declares
neither — `support.docs` and `homepage` can point at the published site — and pass `--repository` only to override
what the manifests declare.

Tell the user about the one-time repository setup the workflows do not do:

```bash
git switch --orphan gh-pages
git commit --allow-empty -m 'docs: create the documentation branch'
git push -u origin gh-pages
git switch <default-branch>
```

Then set Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source to "Deploy from a branch", branch `gh-pages`, folder
`/ (root)`. The site is served at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/`, and previews at
`https://<owner>.github.io/<repository>/pr/<number>/`.

## Verification

After applying:

```bash
composer docgen
```

Exit codes:

- `0`: documentation generated
- `2`: configuration or runtime error

Then preview locally with `vendor/bin/docgen --serve` and spot-check the index page, one class page, and search.

Check the generated package list and source links in normal and diff output. After
narrowing scope, regenerate with the existing cache and verify removed package
pages disappear; publishing must delete stale output too while preserving the
preview directories owned by the other workflow.

When a workflow was installed, check it too, and say plainly that the publishing itself is only observable after the
workflow runs on the default branch:

```bash
go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@latest .github/workflows/docs.yml
```

## References

- [DocGen](vendor/k-kinzal/php-ai-toolkit/docs/docgen.md) — CLI behavior, scope semantics, caching, analysis, and output.

# SQL Parser

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
[![Docs](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-sql--parser-0969da?logo=php&logoColor=white)](https://k-kinzal.github.io/ztd-query-php/k-kinzal/sql-parser/)
[![PHP Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/PHP-8.1%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.php.net/)
[![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/k-kinzal/ztd-query-php)

SQL Parser is a set of LALR(1) parsers for MySQL, PostgreSQL, and SQLite written in PHP. Each parser is generated from the official grammar of a server version (`sql_yacc.yy` for MySQL, `gram.y` for PostgreSQL, and `parse.y` for SQLite), and its lexer is a port of the server's own scanner, so text is tokenized and parsed the way the server does it. The syntax tree names the nonterminals of the upstream grammar, and parsing is lossless: a tree writes back the text it was parsed from, byte for byte, including comments and whitespace.

## Requirements

- PHP 8.1+ with the zlib extension

## Support Syntax

The following grammar versions are bundled. Pass the version tag to the parser; omitting it uses the default for that database.

### MySQL

| Version | Version tag | Default |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| 5.6.51 | `mysql-5.6.51` | |
| 5.7.44 | `mysql-5.7.44` | |
| 8.0.44 | `mysql-8.0.44` | |
| 8.1.0 | `mysql-8.1.0` | |
| 8.2.0 | `mysql-8.2.0` | |
| 8.3.0 | `mysql-8.3.0` | |
| 8.4.7 | `mysql-8.4.7` | Yes |
| 9.0.1 | `mysql-9.0.1` | |
| 9.1.0 | `mysql-9.1.0` | |

### PostgreSQL

| Version | Version tag | Default |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| 17.2 | `pg-17.2` | Yes |

### SQLite

| Version | Version tag | Default |
|---------|-------------|---------|
| 3.47.2 | `sqlite-3.47.2` | Yes |

## Installation

```bash
composer require k-kinzal/sql-parser
```

## Usage

```php
use SqlParser\MySql\MySqlParser;

$parser = new MySqlParser('mysql-8.4.7');
$sql = 'SELECT id, name FROM users u WHERE u.id = ? ORDER BY id LIMIT 10';
$tree = $parser->parse($sql);

$tree->name;                                     // 'start_entry', the grammar's start symbol
$tree->find('where_clause')[0]->text($sql);      // 'WHERE u.id = ?'
$tree->find('table_reference')[0]->text($sql);   // 'users u'
$tree->toString();                               // the statement again, byte for byte
```

## License

MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details.

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Fuzz\Target;

use Error;
use Faker\Factory;
use Faker\Generator;
use SqlCatalog\Facade\Analyzer;
use SqlFaker\Generation\Choice\BytePlanCompiler;
use SqlFaker\Generation\Choice\PlanBuilder;
use SqlFaker\Generation\Plan\GenerationPlan;
use SqlFaker\MySql\MySqlProvider;

/**
 * Checks that a statement written into PHP comes back out of the catalog.
 *
 * The input picks both the statement, through sql-faker's grammar, and the way
 * it is written into the source: as one literal, as a concatenation, through a
 * constant, through a variable, through a call. Every one of those has to
 * produce the same catalogued statement, character for character, because the
 * whole point of the analysis is that how a query is assembled does not change
 * what it is.
 */
final class RecoverTarget
{
    private readonly Generator $faker;

    private readonly MySqlProvider $sql;

    private readonly PlanBuilder $planner;

    /**
     * @var GenerationPlan<bool>
     */
    private readonly GenerationPlan $plan;

    private readonly Analyzer $analyzer;

    /**
     * Builds the target over one grammar version and one expansion budget.
     */
    public function __construct(private readonly string $grammarVersion, int $maxExpansions = 64)
    {
        $this->faker = Factory::create();
        $this->sql = new MySqlProvider($this->faker, $grammarVersion);
        $this->planner = $this->sql->planner();
        $this->plan = GenerationPlan::fromRule('select_stmt')->requiringNonEmpty()->withExpansionBudget($maxExpansions);
        $this->analyzer = new Analyzer();
    }

    /**
     * Writes a generated statement into PHP and checks that it comes back.
     *
     * @throws Error When the catalog does not hold exactly the statement that was written
     */
    public function __invoke(string $input): void
    {
        $plan = (new BytePlanCompiler())->compile($input, $this->planner, $this->plan);
        $statement = $this->sql->generate($plan);
        if ($statement === '') {
            return;
        }

        $shape = strlen($input) === 0 ? 0 : ord($input[0]) % 6;
        $catalog = $this->analyzer->analyzeSource(['fuzz.php' => $this->program($shape, $statement)]);

        if ($catalog->count() !== 1) {
            throw new Error(sprintf(
                'Expected one statement, got %d; shape=%d; input=%s%sSQL: %s',
                $catalog->count(),
                $shape,
                bin2hex($input),
                PHP_EOL,
                $statement,
            ));
        }

        $recovered = $catalog->entries()[0]->pattern->text();
        if ($recovered !== $statement) {
            throw new Error(sprintf(
                'Recovered a different statement; shape=%d; input=%s%sWritten:   %s%sRecovered: %s',
                $shape,
                bin2hex($input),
                PHP_EOL,
                $statement,
                PHP_EOL,
                $recovered ?? '(unresolved)',
            ));
        }
    }

    /**
     * A PHP program that issues the statement, written the way the shape says.
     */
    public function program(int $shape, string $statement): string
    {
        $literal = var_export($statement, true);
        $head = var_export(substr($statement, 0, (int) (strlen($statement) / 2)), true);
        $tail = var_export(substr($statement, (int) (strlen($statement) / 2)), true);

        return '<?php ' . match ($shape) {
            0 => 'function f(\\PDO $d): void { $d->query(' . $literal . '); }',
            1 => 'function f(\\PDO $d): void { $sql = ' . $literal . '; $d->query($sql); }',
            2 => 'function f(\\PDO $d): void { $d->query(' . $head . ' . ' . $tail . '); }',
            3 => 'const Q = ' . $literal . '; function f(\\PDO $d): void { $d->query(Q); }',
            4 => 'class C { public const Q = ' . $literal . '; } function f(\\PDO $d): void { $d->query(C::Q); }',
            default => 'function q(): string { return ' . $literal . '; } function f(\\PDO $d): void { $d->query(q()); }',
        };
    }
}

name: Docs Preview

on:
  pull_request:
    types:
      - opened
      - synchronize
      - reopened
      - closed

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION: '1'
  DOCS_BRANCH: REPLACE_WITH_DOCS_BRANCH

jobs:
  preview:
    name: Generate and publish the pull request preview
    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out the pull request
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Set up PHP
        uses: shivammathur/setup-php@f3e473d116dcccaddc5834248c87452386958240
        with:
          php-version: 'REPLACE_WITH_DOCGEN_JOB_PHP'
          extensions: REPLACE_WITH_REQUIRED_EXTENSIONS
          coverage: pcov

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ramsey/composer-install@65e4f84970763564f46a70b8a54b90d033b3bdda
        with:
          dependency-versions: REPLACE_WITH_DEPENDENCY_MODE
          composer-options: --prefer-dist
          require-lock-file: REPLACE_WITH_LOCK_REQUIREMENT

      - name: Check installed platform requirements
        run: composer check-platform-reqs

      - name: Restore the DocGen cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9
        with:
          path: build/docgen-cache
          key: docgen-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('REPLACE_WITH_SELECTED_LOCK_FILE') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            docgen-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('REPLACE_WITH_SELECTED_LOCK_FILE') }}-
            docgen-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Generate the coverage report the preview reads
        run: vendor/bin/phpunit --coverage-xml build/coverage-xml

      - name: Generate the documentation in diff mode
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          repository="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
          vendor/bin/docgen --coverage=build/coverage-xml --diff="${BASE_SHA}" \
            --base-url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}"

      - name: Check out the documentation branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}
          path: .docs-branch

      - name: Publish the preview
        working-directory: .docs-branch
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          mkdir -p "pr/${PR_NUMBER}"
          rsync -a --checksum --delete ../build/docs/ "pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"
          touch .nojekyll

          git add --all
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch already serves this preview."
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message "docs: preview pull request #${PR_NUMBER} at ${HEAD_SHA}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

      - name: Comment the preview link on the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          repository="$(printf '%s' "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
          preview_url="https://${repository%%/*}.github.io/${repository#*/}/pr/${PR_NUMBER}/"

          gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" --edit-last --create-if-none --body \
          "**Documentation preview:** ${preview_url}

          Generated in diff mode against \`${BASE_REF}\`, so every page marks what this pull
          request adds, removes, and changes; the display-mode switch next to the theme
          toggle shows the plain documentation, the marked documentation, or the changes
          alone.

          Updated for ${HEAD_SHA}. The preview is removed when this pull request is closed."

  cleanup:
    name: Remove the pull request preview
    if: github.event.action == 'closed' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - name: Check out the documentation branch
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.DOCS_BRANCH }}

      - name: Remove the preview
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          rm -rf "pr/${PR_NUMBER}"

          git add --all
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "The ${DOCS_BRANCH} branch carries no preview of this pull request."
            exit 0
          fi

          git -c user.name='github-actions[bot]' \
            -c user.email='41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com' \
            commit --message "docs: remove the preview of pull request #${PR_NUMBER}"
          git push origin "HEAD:${DOCS_BRANCH}"

      - name: Note the removal on the pull request
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          gh pr comment "${PR_NUMBER}" --edit-last --body \
            'The documentation preview of this pull request has been removed.' \
            || echo 'This pull request has no preview comment.'

180	Use the entry point provided by the resolved Deptrac release. Only when that actual
181	release does not expose `vendor/bin/deptrac`, add a project-root launcher such as
182	`deptrac.php` instead of assuming a legacy layout or adding a new file under `bin/`:
183	
184	```php
185	<?php
186	
187	declare(strict_types=1);
188	
189	$deptracEntrypoints = [
190	    __DIR__ . '/vendor/bin/deptrac',
191	    __DIR__ . '/vendor/deptrac/deptrac/deptrac.php',
192	];
193	
194	foreach ($deptracEntrypoints as $deptracEntrypoint) {
195	    if (!is_file($deptracEntrypoint)) {
196	        continue;
197	    }
198	
199	    $command = array_map(
200	        static fn (string $argument): string => escapeshellarg($argument),
201	        [
202	            PHP_BINARY,
203	            $deptracEntrypoint,
204	            ...array_slice($argv, 1),
205	        ],
206	    );
207	
208	    passthru(implode(' ', $command), $exitCode);
209	    exit($exitCode);
210	}
211	
212	fwrite(STDERR, 'Could not find Deptrac. Run "composer install" first.' . PHP_EOL);
213	exit(1);
214	```
215	
216	Then call the launcher from Composer:
217	
218	```json
219	{
220	    "scripts": {
221	        "phpstan": "phpstan analyse --memory-limit=512M",
222	        "deptrac": "@php deptrac.php analyse --config-file=deptrac.yaml",
223	        "lint": [
224	            "@format:check",
225	            "@phpstan",
226	            "@deptrac"
227	        ]
228	    }
229	}
230	```
231	
232	If the project already has `lint` or `check`, merge `@deptrac` into it after PHPStan unless runtime constraints require Deptrac to run in a separate CI job. Do not remove existing lint steps.
233	
234	## Verification
235	
236	After applying:
237	
238	```bash
239	composer deptrac
240	php deptrac.php debug:unassigned --config-file=deptrac.yaml
241	php deptrac.php debug:unused --config-file=deptrac.yaml
242	```
243	
244	`debug:unassigned` can return a non-zero exit code when it successfully finds unassigned tokens. Treat the output as a collector coverage report, not as a command failure by itself.
245	
246	Fix configuration in this order:
247	
248	1. Syntax/config errors.
249	2. Unassigned production tokens.
250	3. Unused rulesets caused by stale layer assumptions.
251	4. Real architecture violations.
252	
253	Use disposable dependencies to verify the important forbidden directions really
254	fail, including a shared stage referring to a concrete adapter. A zero-violation
255	report alone does not prove that collectors enforce the intended boundaries.
256
